issues.title: Persistent keyspace USE failure retries forever, leaving pool permanently Broken
issues.verdictReason: current_keyspace is set once by use_keyspace() and never cleared on failure; the new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace(err)) arm at connection_pool.rs:900 discards the connection and, via run()'s need_filling()/refill_delay_strategy at lines 723-739, keeps scheduling refills with backoff forever. For a non-transient failure (dropped/nonexistent keyspace, revoked permission) every refill repeats the same failing USE and the pool stays Broken permanently, whereas base code (removed in this diff) only warn!-logged and still admitted the connection so fully-qualified queries kept working.
issues.scopeReason: The discard-on-keyspace-failure behavior and the resulting permanent-Broken state are newly introduced by this PR's handle_ready_connection change.

issues.title: Missing timeout on per-connection USE means a hung request delays the new Broken report…
issues.verdictReason: start_setting_keyspace_for_connection (line ~1336) has an explicit `// TODO: There should be a timeout for this` and calls connection.use_keyspace() with no timeout wrapper, unlike the pool-wide use_keyspace() which does wrap with tokio::time::timeout. A hung USE keeps its future in ready_connections, so is_filling() (line 744) stays true indefinitely, which blocks the new `if !self.is_filling() && self.is_empty()` check at line 908 from ever firing - the new Broken-reporting path this PR adds never triggers.
issues.scopeReason: The missing timeout itself predates the PR, but the new failure-reporting branch this PR adds is what first creates a dependency on that hung future ever completing.

issues.title: Keyspace-mismatch check now runs before resharding/shard-aware-port update, undocumented…
issues.verdictReason: Diffed handle_ready_connection: the keyspace-mismatch check and early return (now lines 913-929) moved from after to before the 'Update sharding and optionally reshard' block (maybe_reshard call and shard_aware_port update). Previously every newly opened connection updated sharder/shard_aware_port immediately on arrival; now, whenever current_keyspace is set and a connection still needs its USE applied, it returns early via start_setting_keyspace_for_connection and skips those updates until a later Ok event with a matching keyspace_name arrives. During a sustained keyspace failure (the new feature this PR adds) sharder/shard_aware_port never update at all - the new test literally asserts `refiller.sharder.is_none()` after such a failure - and the PR description does not mention this reordering or its staleness window.
issues.scopeReason: The reordering of the keyspace check relative to resharding is a direct hunk in this PR's diff.
